speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a pruritic rash on your bilateral upper extremities. To help me determine the cause, how long has this rash been present, and have you noticed any new soaps, detergents, or plants in your environment recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given the 5-month duration and bilateral distribution on your upper extremities without clear external triggers, have you noticed any other symptoms like fever, joint pain, or fatigue, and does the rash change color or texture in response to heat?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on the bilateral upper extremities. I also have No fever, No joint pains, No recent illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Polymorphous Light Eruption (PMLE).

The chronic, pruritic rash on your upper extremities without fever or joint pain, combined with the lack of response to avoidance or new substances, is highly suggestive of a photosensitivity disorder. Since the rash worsens with heat, I am confident in this diagnosis.
